title: S.A.M Custom Playable Race
description: A mod-defined playable race that rides an existing monster body. Registered into a reserved race id (200-255); appears in the character-select race picker, renders as its host body in both third- and first-person, and applies flat attribute/HP/MP bonuses at character creation. A vanilla or mod-less client that loads such a character plays it as Human (graceful degrade).

name.description: Display name shown in the character-select race picker, on its info card, on the main-menu leaderboards, (from 3.8.1) on the race line of the in-game character sheet and (from 3.11.0) as the title of the race's page in the compendium and (from 3.12.2) wherever the game calls the player by kind: what a human or shopkeeper says on turning on them ("Foul Frostborn! En Guarde!"), the Wanted tooltip and the line another player reads on examining them, e.g. "Frostborn".

host_body.description: The existing monster body this race renders as. Only these 18 bodies have a proper first-person arm, so both views are correct.

description.description: Short flavour text for the race (shown in the picker's info panel and, from 3.8.1, in the tooltip of the race line on the in-game character sheet, and (from 3.11.0) on the race's page in the compendium, a line for each line break, unless the race has lore).

lore.description: (from 3.12.0) Text for the box under the model on this race's page in the Dungeon Compendium, in place of description, which stays in the character-select picker and the character sheet's tooltip. Each line break (\n) starts a new line, and a line too long for the box is wrapped. The box was made for the game's own texts, which are about six short lines. Leave it out to show description there.

icon.description: (From 3.9.0.) Mod-relative path to a small PNG (about 32 by 32 pixels) used as this race's picture on the saved-game cards and, in a co-op game, on the status bars of the other players, in place of the host body's icon, e.g. "races/frostborn.png". Write it from the folder that holds mod.json, with no leading slash. A path the game cannot find, or one that climbs out of the mod folder, is reported in sam_log.txt and the body's icon is kept.

stat_modifiers.description: Flat attribute / HP / MP bonuses added at character creation (may be negative). Vanilla races give no attribute bonuses, so these are the race's whole stat identity.

blood_diet.description: If true, this race sustains on blood instead of food (like a vampire).

vision.description: How much further this race sees in the dark, in tiles of the player's own light radius, wherever Perception's light bonus goes (every light the player carries, sneaking or not). Added in full on top of Perception's own bonus; with VISION stat modifiers, S.A.M's whole part is capped at -4..6. Ignored when the player turns race abilities off at character creation.

sneak_vision.description: Extra light radius, in tiles, while sneaking without a light source: the Gremlin's Improved Sneak Vision is 2. A race on the gremlin body already gets that +2 from the engine, and this is added to it. With SNEAK_VISION stat modifiers, S.A.M's whole part is capped at -6..6. Ignored when the player turns race abilities off at character creation.

recruits.description: (new in 3.7.0) Monster types this race can recruit as followers by pressing Use on them, such as ["rat", "spider"]. The game normally decides who you may recruit from your BODY: a human body recruits what is friendly, a spider body recruits spiders, scarabs and scorpions, and so on. This list adds types on top of that for any body, and it keeps working at Legendary Leadership (100), where the body table alone decides. A listed type is also your ally: the game counts it as a friend and not an enemy, unless the same type is under enemies or neutral: those win, and the type is dropped from this list with a warning. Your Leadership still limits how many followers you can have. Creatures that can never be made followers (bosses, shopkeepers, mimics, the tinkering bots, holograms, bats) are not in the list. Ignored while the player has monster abilities turned off. It does not look at shapeshifting.

can_open_tins.description: If true, this race opens a tin without a tin opener. It eats one, as a Goatman or an Automaton does (a race on either of those bodies already can eat one), and (from 3.12.1) it puts one in at the cooking screen of a cauldron or frying pan, where the game's own Goatman and Automaton still need an opener. Ignored when the player turns race abilities off at character creation.

emote_sounds.description: (from 3.13.0) What this race says when its player presses Use on nothing, in place of its host body's noise (a salamander growls, a dryad creaks, the human body says nothing). Sound ids: a bare name is one of your own ("purr" = "<namespace>:purr"), "namespace:name" any mod's. One plays at random, at most once every five seconds on every body, and in multiplayer the other players hear one too, picked on their own machine (read in the code). A race that lists sounds never makes its body's noise: an id no loaded mod registers is silent. Only in the race's own body: with "disable monster abilities" ticked, or while polymorphed or shapeshifted, the game's own noise stays.

starting_spells.description: Innate spells this race knows from creation. Vanilla "SPELL_X" names or your own "namespace:spell". They are also put on the first free hotbar slots when the character is created.

starting_items.description: Items a character of this race starts with (from 3.15.0), whatever their class, given after the class's own starting items. The entries are the same as a class's starting_items. Only when the race is played with its abilities: a character who picked the race for its look alone gets none, as with starting_spells.

type.description: Item to grant: a vanilla ItemType name (e.g. 'IRON_AXE') or a custom S.A.M item id in 'namespace:item' form.

status.description: Item condition (Barony Status enum, from items.hpp). Note the Barony spelling 'SERVICABLE'.

beatitude.description: Blessedness: negative = cursed, 0 = uncursed, positive = blessed.

count.description: How many of the item to grant (stack size).

appearance.description: Which look the item has, counting from 0. Many items have several looks (a plain cloak has 4, so 0 to 3; most hats 2 to 4; a ring 5; a potion up to 8); a number past the last wraps around. For a READABLE_BOOK it is the book index (0-33 in vanilla), choosing which book it is. Leave it at 0 on a spell tome, a spellbook, a spell item, a scroll of mail, an enchanted feather, a scepter, a loot bag and the four robots: there it is game data or has no effect. The Class Editor has a Look picker for the items that have several looks.

equip.description: If true, auto-equip the item on start (weapons/armor/rings); if false, place it in the inventory.

hotbar_slot.description: Hotbar slot (0-9) to bind this item to, or -1 for none. Works together with equip: true: an equipped item with a hotbar_slot starts in the hand (or on the body) and on that hotbar key, the way the Wizard starts with the quarterstaff. Slot 0 is hotbar key 1.

allies.description: Monster types that will not attack this race, and that this race will not attack, on top of whatever the host body already gets along with. A goatman-bodied race is already left alone by goatmen; this is for relations the host body does NOT have, e.g. ["gnome", "troll"]. Leave it out to inherit the host body's relations unchanged.

enemies.description: Monster types that are always hostile to this race, even ones the host body gets along with. Listing a type in both allies and enemies makes it an enemy, and the game log says so.

neutral.description: Monster types that are NEUTRAL to this race: they will not attack it on sight and it is not their ally, the relation a Gremlin has with Goblins. Use it to take a type out of the host body's allies without making it hostile, for example a human-bodied race that humans leave alone and cannot recruit. A neutral creature that is attacked still fights back. At Legendary Leadership (100) the game recruits by body type and ignores every allegiance list, so from then on a neutral type can be recruited, as a Gremlin can recruit Goblins. A shopkeeper listed here will trade, except while you are shapeshifted (as in vanilla). A type in more than one list gets the least friendly: enemies, then neutral, then allies.

limb_models.description: This race's own body, one model per limb, instead of the host body's. host_body still decides the skeleton: the limb offsets, the animation, and which slots exist. These decide what is drawn in each slot. Omit a limb and it keeps the host body's model, so you can replace just a head or the whole body. Every limb except the head is only visible when that armour slot is empty, which is how every race in the game already works.

head.description: The head. This is the one limb no armour ever replaces, so it always shows. Four forms are accepted, in the order they are tried: a path to a model the game already has ("gharbad_head.vox", or the full "models/creatures/..." form if that filename is used by more than one creature); an id you declared in mod.json "models" ("<ns>:name"); a mod-relative path to your own .vox; or a raw model index. Prefer a path: an index says nothing about what it is, and models.txt line N is index N-1, which is easy to get wrong by one. You may also give an object with a "model" key, for consistency with the other slots, but the head has no transform: the engine sets it outside the limb path, so scale/offset/pitch/roll on head are reported and ignored.

torso.description: The chest. Shown bare; a breastplate covers it, exactly as it does for any other race. Four forms are accepted, in the order they are tried: a path to a model the game already has ("gharbad_head.vox", or the full "models/creatures/..." form if that filename is used by more than one creature); an id you declared in mod.json "models" ("<ns>:name"); a mod-relative path to your own .vox; or a raw model index. Prefer a path: an index says nothing about what it is, and models.txt line N is index N-1, which is easy to get wrong by one. Instead of a bare string you may give an object: { "model": "...", "scale": 1.2, "offset": { "x": 0, "y": 0, "z": -1 }, "pitch": 0, "roll": 0 }. Use that when your race's proportions differ from the host body's and the limb clips or floats; a bare string keeps the host body's proportions.

model.description: The .vox for this limb. Same four forms a bare string accepts.

scale.description: Uniform scale for this limb. 1.0 = the model's own size.

offset.description: Shift the limb in its OWN frame, so it stays correct as the limb swings.

pitch.description: Extra pitch in radians, added to whatever the animation set.

roll.description: Extra roll in radians, added to whatever the animation set.

arm_right.description: The right arm. Shown bare; sleeves and gloves cover it. Four forms are accepted, in the order they are tried: a path to a model the game already has ("gharbad_head.vox", or the full "models/creatures/..." form if that filename is used by more than one creature); an id you declared in mod.json "models" ("<ns>:name"); a mod-relative path to your own .vox; or a raw model index. Prefer a path: an index says nothing about what it is, and models.txt line N is index N-1, which is easy to get wrong by one. Instead of a bare string you may give an object: { "model": "...", "scale": 1.2, "offset": { "x": 0, "y": 0, "z": -1 }, "pitch": 0, "roll": 0 }. Use that when your race's proportions differ from the host body's and the limb clips or floats; a bare string keeps the host body's proportions. To make the arm bend when it holds something, use the object form and give it a "bent" key beside "model": { "model": "mymod:arm_right", "bent": "mymod:arm_right_bent" }. "bent" is a plain string like "model" is, the model of the arm drawn while that hand is full.

model.description: The .vox for this limb. Same four forms a bare string accepts.

scale.description: Uniform scale for this limb. 1.0 = the model's own size.

offset.description: Shift the limb in its OWN frame, so it stays correct as the limb swings.

pitch.description: Extra pitch in radians, added to whatever the animation set.

roll.description: Extra roll in radians, added to whatever the animation set.

bent.description: The same arm, drawn while that hand is holding something: a weapon in the right hand, a shield or lantern in the left, and during a spell windup. Same four forms as "model". Without it your arm keeps one pose forever, because the base game reaches a bent arm by stepping two entries forward in its own model list (ArmRight, ArmLeft, ArmBentRight, ArmBentLeft) and your arm is a single added model with nothing reserved after it. Leave the arms out of limb_models entirely and you get the host body's arms, which bend on their own.

first_person.description: What YOU see of your own body. Everyone else sees the limb_models above; without this you would see the host body's arms, which is the first thing a player of a custom race notices. Never networked: these are drawn only on your own machine.

arm.description: The forearm/hand that holds your weapon. Also used for the right casting hand, which vanilla draws with the same model.

hand_left.description: The left casting hand, a different model from the arm in every vanilla race too.

extra_limbs.description: Limbs the host body does not have: a tail, wings, horns, extra arms. Barony allocates 29 limb slots per player and uses 16, so there are exactly 13 spare. Drawn on every machine, so all players see them.

attach.description: What it hangs off. body = the player's centre, offset in the direction they face (how the salamander tail works). head = follows the head, like a mask. torso = follows the chest limb.

offset.description: Where to put it, in the direction the player faces.

up.description: A positive number moves the limb DOWN: the engine's height runs downward, and an extra limb's offset uses it as it is.

focal.description: Moves the model away from the point it turns about, in the limb's own directions: x forward, y right, z DOWN, in world units (a voxel is half a unit). The limb turns about where it is placed (its attach point moved by its offset); with no focal or root that is the model's own middle, so a tail turns about its middle. Prefer "root", which works the numbers out from the model. With a root, focal is added on top as a nudge.

root.description: (from 3.10.0) Which end of the model joins the body: the average position of the voxels on that side's outermost layer (empty space in the .vox does not count) is put where the limb is placed, so it turns and sways about that end instead of its own middle. A tail that hangs from the torso is "top", one that stands up is "bottom", one that sticks out behind is "front". From 3.10.1, a tail whose top layer is only the part that meets the body pivots there; in 3.10.0 root used the middle of the whole side. Top and bottom are as you see the model in game; front, back, left and right are the model's own, so they turn with yaw_offset.

yaw_offset.description: Degrees, if the .vox was authored facing a different way.

sway.description: Swing it as the player moves. true or "tilt": the salamander tail's motion, up and down with a slight twist, which reads as a swish only on a model built like that tail. "side" (from 3.9.1): the far end swings to the player's left and right about the point the limb turns about. Give the limb a "root" so that point is the end that joins the body; without root or focal it is the model's middle, and the limb only turns in place. From 3.10.0, with a root or focal, a limb that hangs down or stands up now swings like a pendulum, and one that sticks out behind swings side to side. Good for tails, wrong for horns.

itemType.description: A vanilla Barony ItemType enum name (from items.hpp).
